title: Mutation testing in practice using Ruby
authors: Li, N.; West, M.; Escalona, A.; Durelli, V.H.S.
venue: 2015 IEEE Eighth International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW)
supporting_sentence: Second, we applied mutation testing to an industrial Ruby project at Medidata and reported the lessons learned from the study.
relevance: Closest prior work: mutation testing on an industrial Ruby project; single proprietary case study, no public corpus, no BDD-layer isolation, no longitudinal component.

title: Skyfire: Model-Based Testing with Cucumber
authors: Li, N.; Escalona, A.; Kamal, T.
venue: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Software Testing Verification and Validation (ICST)
supporting_sentence: More importantly, practitioners do not have a metric to measure test coverage.
relevance: States that Cucumber practitioners lack metrics for their scenarios; motivates a BDD-level oracle-strength metric, though the paper supplies none.

title: Will my tests tell me if I break this code?
authors: Niedermayr, R.; Juergens, E.; Wagner, S.
venue: 2016 IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Continuous Software Evolution and Delivery (CSED)
supporting_sentence: The results show that the ratio of pseudo-tested methods is acceptable for unit tests but not for system tests (that execute large portions of the whole system).
relevance: Separates mutation-based adequacy by test level (unit vs system); the single biggest threat to novelty of our test-level differential analysis.

title: A comprehensive study of pseudo-tested methods
authors: Vera-Pérez, O.L.; Danglot, B.; Monperrus, M.; Baudry, B.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: pseudo-tested methods are significantly less tested than the other methods; yet, for most of them, the developers would not pay the testing price to fix this situation.
relevance: 28K+ method replication of extreme-mutation oracle weakness; establishes coverage can mask weak oracles, at unit level only.

title: Mutation Analysis for Assessing End-to-End Web Tests
authors: Yandrapally, R.; Mesbah, A.
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME)
supporting_sentence: We evaluate our dynamic mutation analysis framework on six open source web apps.
relevance: Mutation analysis of E2E/UI suites over six public web apps: higher-level mutation at scale already exists, but not scoped to BDD layers or history.

title: Mutta: a novel tool for E2E web mutation testing
authors: Leotta, M.; Paparella, D.; Ricca, F.
venue: Software Quality Journal
supporting_sentence: In detail, Mutta has been executed on two web applications, each equipped with different test suites to compare assertions with differential testing.
relevance: E2E mutation that compares two oracle styles (assertions vs differential); closest existing work to 'oracle strength of acceptance tests'.

title: Data-Driven Mutation Analysis for Cyber-Physical Systems
authors: Viganò, E.; Cornejo, O.; Pastore, F.; Briand, L.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: Our results show that the approach effectively detects test suite shortcomings, is not affected by equivalent and redundant mutants, and entails acceptable costs.
relevance: Mutation above unit level on black-box/interoperability interfaces; shows system-level mutation is an accepted idea in other domains.

title: Keeping Mutation Test Suites Consistent and Relevant with Long-Standing Mutants
authors: Ojdanić, M.; Papadakis, M.; Harman, M.
venue: Proceedings of the 31st ACM Joint European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering (ESEC/FSE)
supporting_sentence: We measure this degradation in relevance for 143,500 mutants in 4 non-trivial systems, finding that 52% degrade, on average.
relevance: The closest longitudinal mutation study: mutant relevance degrades over history; not BDD, not oracle strength, no drift-indicator validation.

title: Is mutation an appropriate tool for testing experiments?
authors: Andrews, J.H.; Briand, L.C.; Labiche, Y.
venue: Proceedings of the 27th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
supporting_sentence: It is concluded that, based on the data available thus far, the use of mutation operators is yielding trustworthy results (generated mutants are similar to real faults).
relevance: Defends mutants as real-fault proxies; required to justify using mutation score as ground truth in our design.

title: An Analysis and Survey of the Development of Mutation Testing
authors: Jia, Y.; Harman, M.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis and survey of Mutation Testing.
relevance: Canonical mutation-testing survey; documents the field's historical concentration on code-level/unit mutation.

title: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey
authors: Barr, E.T.; Harman, M.; McMinn, P.; Shahbaz, M.; Yoo, S.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: Given an input for a system, the challenge of distinguishing the corresponding desired, correct behaviour from potentially incorrect behavior is called the “test oracle problem”.
relevance: Canonical oracle-problem survey; frames oracle automation as the bottleneck but never quantifies oracle strength of BDD suites.

title: Maintaining behaviour driven development specifications: Challenges and opportunities
authors: Binamungu, L.P.; Embury, S.M.; Konstantinou, N.
venue: 2018 IEEE 25th International Conference on Software Analysis Evolution and Reengineering (SANER)
supporting_sentence: The results also showed that BDD specifications suffer the same maintenance challenges found in automated test suites more generally.
relevance: Survey of 75 BDD practitioners: establishes BDD specification drift/maintenance as a real problem, with no fault-based measurement.

title: Detecting duplicate examples in behaviour driven development specifications
authors: Binamungu, L.P.; Embury, S.M.; Konstantinou, N.
venue: 2018 IEEE Workshop on Validation Analysis and Evolution of Software Tests (VST)
supporting_sentence: We present an approach for detecting duplication in BDD suites that is based around dynamic tracing, and describe an evaluation based on three open source systems.
relevance: Structural quality metric for BDD suites evaluated on public systems; the kind of non-fault-based metric our mutation-based measure is contrasted with.

title: Behaviour driven development: A systematic mapping study
authors: Binamungu, L.P.; Maro, S.
venue: Journal of Systems and Software
supporting_sentence: acute shortage of metrics for measuring various aspects of BDD specifications and the processes for producing BDD specifications
relevance: 166-paper mapping study of BDD (2006-2021): the word 'mutation' appears nowhere in the full text; names metrics for BDD specs as the key gap.

title: How to Evaluate BDD Scenarios' Quality?
authors: Oliveira, G.; Marczak, S.; Moralles, C.
venue: Proceedings of the XXXIII Brazilian Symposium on Software Engineering (SBES)
supporting_sentence: To address this lack of guidance, we define a set of quality attributes and propose a question-based checklist to assist BDD scenarios' quality evaluations.
relevance: Operational quality checklist for BDD scenarios from 18 practitioners; qualitative/structural, never validated against fault detection.

title: Predicting Co-Changes between Functionality Specifications and Source Code in Behavior Driven Development
authors: Yang, A.Z.H.; Alencar da Costa, D.; Zou, Y.
venue: 2019 IEEE/ACM 16th International Conference on Mining Software Repositories (MSR)
supporting_sentence: Therefore, .feature files can be out-of-date, reducing the advantages of using BDD.
relevance: Closest drift work: predicts BDD feature-file/code co-changes (AUC 0.77) but never validates the predictor against fault-detection ground truth.

title: A dataset of regressions in web applications detected by end-to-end tests
authors: Soto-Sánchez, Ó.; Maes-Bermejo, M.; Gallego, M.; Gortázar, F.
venue: Software Quality Journal
supporting_sentence: The comparative study shows that there are important differences between end-to-end and unit tests, such as their execution time and the amount of resources they consume, which are much higher in the end-to-end tests.
relevance: Documents the cost asymmetry of E2E suites; justifies our measuring oracle strength without executing whole E2E suites at scale.

title: An Empirical Study on Mutation Statement and Branch Coverage Fault Revelation That Avoids the Unreliable Clean Program Assumption
authors: Titcheu Chekam, T.; Papadakis, M.; Le Traon, Y.; Harman, M.
venue: Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
supporting_sentence: our primary finding is that strong mutation testing has the highest fault revelation of four widely-used criteria.
relevance: Mutation score beats statement/branch coverage at revealing real faults; grounds its use as the oracle-strength ground truth.

title: Test suites effectiveness evolution in open source systems: empirical study
authors: Akour, M.; Alenezi, M.
venue: Indonesian Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
supporting_sentence: In this work, the code coverage, test suite LOC and mutation testing coverage are measured to assess the correlation between the effectiveness of fault detection, code coverage, and test suite size.
relevance: Mutation coverage tracked across 11 versions of 3 OSS Java systems: longitudinal mutation exists, but unit-level, no BDD, no per-layer split.

title: Test Co-Evolution in Software Projects: A Large-Scale Empirical Study
authors: Miranda, C.; Avelino, G.A.; Santos Neto, P.
venue: Journal of Software: Evolution and Process
supporting_sentence: The asynchronous evolution of tests and code can compromise software quality and project longevity.
relevance: 526-repository longitudinal test co-evolution study; measures synchrony of change, never oracle strength or fault detection.

title: Test-driven development with mutation testing – an experimental study
authors: Roman, A.; Mnich, M.
venue: Software Quality Journal
supporting_sentence: The TDD+M tests achieved better coverage on the code from TDD groups than the TDD tests on their own code (53.3% vs. 33.5% statement coverage and 64.9% vs. 37.5% mutation coverage).
relevance: Precedent for mutation coverage as the outcome measure of test-suite quality in a controlled experiment (unit level).

title: Mutation operators for specifications
authors: Black, P.E.; Okun, V.; Yesha, Y.
venue: Proceedings of the 15th IEEE International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
supporting_sentence: We define an extensive set of mutation operators for use with this method.
relevance: Mutating the specification (not the code) to generate tests; distinct from our use of code mutation to grade the suite's oracles.

title: AAT4IRS: automated acceptance testing for industrial robotic systems
authors: dos Santos, M.G.; Hallé, S.; Petrillo, F.; Guéhéneuc, Y.-G.
venue: Frontiers in Robotics and AI
supporting_sentence: We evaluated our ST approach through a proof-of-concept, performing a pick-and-place process and applying mutation testing to measure its effectiveness.
